# Token service

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P2 · Proven identity](../README.md#phase-2--proven-identity) · **Lane:** Control plane · **Label:** `feature:token-exchange` · **Epic:** [#81](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/81) · **Tickets:** 7 (2S 5M)

Adds an RFC 8693 token-exchange endpoint on the CP. It turns a user's IdP ID token plus an agent's private_key_jwt assertion into a short-lived Warden token (at most 15 minutes, never longer than the ID token). The token is bound to the agent, so workers trust one CP-signed token instead of verifying raw IdP tokens. Off by default; it is a CP-local `tokenService:` block and nothing changes on the wire while it is disabled.

## How we build it

- Endpoint: `POST /oauth2/token` on the CP mux (`Server.Handler()` in internal/controlplane/controlplane.go). It is form-encoded, the body is capped at 32 KiB (a P1 subject token can be 16 KiB), and every response carries `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Pragma: no-cache`. Parameters: grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange, subject_token, subject_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token, client_assertion_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:client-assertion-type:jwt-bearer, client_assertion, an optional audience (only `warden-worker`, otherwise invalid_target), an optional requested_token_type (only ...:jwt or ...:access_token) and an optional scope. resource and actor_token are rejected, as are duplicate parameters, parameters in the query string and any Authorization header. `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` (RFC 8414) advertises issuer, token_endpoint, jwks_uri (the p2-key-manager `/.well-known/jwks.json`), grant_types_supported, token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported=[private_key_jwt] and token_endpoint_auth_signing_alg_values_supported=[EdDSA, ES256].
- Agent authentication (private_key_jwt) in new package internal/tokensvc, with compact-JWS helpers in new internal/keys/jws.go. The assertion is at most 8 KiB. A kid header is required and must equal a registry JWK's kid or its RFC 7638 thumbprint (agentreg.Store.Get, W-P2-AREG-01). alg is bound to the key type: EdDSA for OKP Ed25519, ES256 for EC P-256. none, HS*, RS*, mismatched algs and the jwk/jku/x5u/x5c/crit headers are rejected before any key is used. Claims: iss==sub==agent id; aud is a single value equal to `tokenService.issuer` or `<issuer>/oauth2/token`, always taken from config and never from the Host header; exp and iat are required; exp-iat <= 5m; iat and nbf are at most 60s in the future; jti is 1-128 printable characters. Replay protection uses cpstate `token_assertion_jti(agent_id, jti_hash, expires_at, PRIMARY KEY(agent_id, jti_hash))`. The row is inserted only after the signature and time checks pass, with one INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, and rows are purged after exp+60s. Unknown agent, unknown kid, bad signature and disabled agent all return the same 401 invalid_client. The bounded reason is kept only in logs and metrics.
- Subject validation: one `identity.NewOIDCVerifier` (W-P1-VRFY-01). It is built at startup from the CP's served `identity` settings block (issuer, audience, jwksURL, groupsClaim, clockSkewSeconds, maxTokenTTLSeconds), so the CP and the workers trust the same IdP. AllowedAZP is overridden by `tokenService.allowedAZP` (default [agent-harness]), so ID tokens minted for other clients cannot be exchanged. Only Status valid continues, and `identity.SubjectFrom(claims, status)` must return a non-nil subject. expired -> invalid_grant/subject_expired; invalid, malformed or too_large -> invalid_grant/subject_invalid; unverified (jwks_unavailable) -> 503 temporarily_unavailable/idp_unavailable with Retry-After, so harnesses retry instead of re-logging in. The verifier accepts only the IdP issuer, so a Warden token can never be a subject_token and `act` is never nested.
- Pluggable subject types: `Service.Exchange` dispatches on subject_token_type through a `SubjectResolver` map. A resolver returns a verified subject, a subject expiry and extra claims. P2 registers id_token; W-P4-DGR-04 later adds `urn:warden:params:token-type:grant` without rewriting Exchange. Any other type returns invalid_request/unsupported_token_type. The common checks and minting run once, after the resolver.
- Authorization, in this order. (1) The agent is active (re-read after the assertion). (2) The user is not blocked: a tokensvc-owned `BlockChecker` interface, implemented in internal/controlplane over `controlplane.BlockStore` (W-P1-BLOCK-03) and its in-memory snapshot (W-P1-BLOCK-07), never over a policy version. It matches sub exactly, and lowercase email only when EmailVerified; a match gives invalid_grant/user_blocked, and a read error gives 503 temporarily_unavailable/block_store_unavailable, never an allow. (3) The subject's groups intersect the agent's allowed_groups, otherwise unauthorized_client/group_not_allowed. (4) Scope is space-delimited tokens matching `^[a-z0-9:._-]{1,64}$`, at most 16. Issued scope is the requested scope when it is a subset of the agent's allowed_scopes (W-P2-AREG-01), or all of allowed_scopes when none is requested, and no scope claim when the list is empty; anything else gives invalid_scope/scope_not_allowed. Errors use RFC 6749/8693 codes, and error_description is only a reason from a closed enum.
- Issued JWT, signed with the internal/keys purpose=token active Signer (W-P2-KEYS-02). Header: alg (from Signer.Alg()), kid, typ=`wt+jwt`. Claims: ver=1, iss=tokenService.issuer, aud=warden-worker, sub, idp_iss (the subject's iss), email and email_verified (only when the email is verified), groups (sorted, as verified), groups_truncated (from Claims.GroupsTruncated), act={sub: agent id}, sid, idp_sid (when the ID token carries one), jti (128-bit crypto/rand, base64url), iat, nbf=iat, exp=min(iat+tokenService.ttl, subject exp), scope (omitted when empty), cnf={jkt: RFC 7638 thumbprint of the JWK that verified the assertion}. Tokens whose encoding would exceed 12 KiB are refused with token_too_large, which keeps them under the worker's 16 KiB cap. keys.ErrNoActiveKey gives 503 temporarily_unavailable/signer_unavailable. Response: access_token, issued_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt, token_type=Bearer, expires_in=exp-iat, scope.
- Token sessions: cpstate `token_sessions(sid TEXT PRIMARY KEY, idp_iss, sub, agent_id, created_at, last_used_at, revoked_at)`, unique on (idp_iss, sub, agent_id) while revoked_at IS NULL, migration id `tokensvc/0002`. This table is separate from the W-P1-SSO-04 console `sessions` table. sid is `wts_` plus 128-bit crypto/rand base64url, so no ULID dependency is needed. A sid is reused per (idp_iss, sub, agent) until it has been idle for 12h, reaches its 7d absolute lifetime, or is revoked. Admins can revoke one session (`POST /dashboard/api/token-sessions/{sid}/revoke`) or all sessions for a sub or an agent (`POST /dashboard/api/token-sessions/revoke`). These are admin-role routes in the W-P1-SSO-05 table, audited through the W-P1-AAUD-02 middleware, and after a revoke the token service refuses exchanges whose subject token was issued at or before the revoke (invalid_grant/session_revoked), which forces a fresh sign-in. Live tokens are stopped by the block list, agent disable or emergency key rotation, within one bundle cycle or the TTL.
- Binding semantics, documented in docs/identity-contract.md: the Warden token is a bearer token bound to the agent through act.sub and cnf.jkt, which workers (p2-worker-bound) check against the listener's agent and the registry key thumbprints. It is not proof of possession. Anyone holding the token can use it from that agent's listener until it expires, and real upstream credentials still never reach the agent. Proof of possession arrives with agent mTLS (cnf x5t#S256).
- Abuse limits, applied in order. (a) A per-client-IP limiter (default 120/minute) runs before parsing; the client IP is RemoteAddr unless the peer is in console.trustedProxies, as in W-P1-AAUD-02. A global in-flight cap (default 64) also applies. (b) A per-agent bucket (default 300/minute, sized for one shared harness agent) is charged only after the assertion verifies. (c) A per-user bucket keyed on (idp_iss, sub) (default 30/minute) is charged only after the subject verifies. A forged iss therefore cannot drain a real agent's budget. All limits return 429 with an integer Retry-After. They use an exported `policy.ParseRateLimit` grammar (`N/second|minute|hour`) with token-bucket semantics, implemented in internal/tokensvc because go.mod has no golang.org/x/time. Each limiter map is LRU-bounded to 10k keys. Limits apply per CP replica.
- Recording. Machine issuance stays out of the hash-chained admin audit. That chain is for admin actions, and P1 never chains requests without a session. Every authenticated outcome (issued, or denied after the assertion verified) writes a cpstate `token_events(id, ts, outcome, reason, agent_id, sub_hmac, sid, jti, kid, exp, scope)` row (migration `tokensvc/0003`; sub_hmac is HMAC-SHA256 with a per-CP salt stored in cpstate) and emits one slog JSON line `msg=token_exchange schema=warden.token.v1` with sub, agent, sid, jti, outcome and reason. If the row cannot be written, the response is 503 temporarily_unavailable/event_store_unavailable and no token is released. Unauthenticated failures write no row; they get a rate-limited WARN line and a counter. Rows are pruned after `tokenService.eventRetention` (default 720h) from the existing retention ticker in `Server.Start`. Session revokes and other admin actions go through adminaudit. subject_token, client_assertion and the issued token are never logged or stored.
- Metrics: the CP has no meter or /metrics endpoint until W-P5-RETN-06. Following the W-P1-WTOK-02 pattern, a nil-safe `tokensvc.Metrics` keeps in-memory counters `warden_cp_tokens_issued_total{agent}` and `warden_cp_tokens_denied_total{reason}` and a `warden_cp_token_exchange_seconds` histogram. reason comes from the closed tokensvc enum, and agent is a registered id or `unknown`. sub and email are never labels. Totals appear in a console token-service summary until W-P5-RETN-06 exports them.
- Config and back-compat: a CP-local `tokenService:` block with `json:"-"`, never on policyWire or SettingsWire. It is accepted by rawConfig under KnownFields(true) and read only from the operator `--config` through new `config.LoadTokenService`, the same pattern as `config.LoadConsole` (W-P1-SSO-02). Keys: enabled (default false), issuer (absolute https URL with no trailing slash; http only for loopback or with allowInsecureIssuer), ttl (default 15m, range 1m-15m), assertionMaxAge (5m), clockSkew (60s), allowedAZP ([agent-harness]), session {idle: 12h, absolute: 168h}, rateLimit {perIP, perAgent, perUser, maxInFlight} and eventRetention (720h). There is no CLI flag. Startup fails when the block is enabled without --state-dir, without a served `identity` issuer, or without a loadable token KeySet. When disabled, /oauth2/token and the discovery document return 404, no tokensvc tables are created, and /policy is byte-identical.
- Degraded modes. No active token key (secret backend or KMS down): 503 temporarily_unavailable and /healthz degraded. IdP unreachable: the cached JWKS still verifies known kids, and an unknown kid or a cold cache gives 503 idp_unavailable. Block store or event store error: 503. A CP restart keeps replay protection and sessions because both are in cpstate, behind `tokensvc.ReplayStore` and `tokensvc.SessionStore` interfaces that p5-postgres-ha can implement. Assertions and subjects get 60s of clock skew; minted tokens get the worker's `identity.clockSkewSeconds` leeway (default 60s, W-P2-WBND-01). In require mode, a CP outage longer than the TTL minus the harness refresh lead (about 5 minutes with refresh at 2/3) stops that agent's traffic. This is documented as accepted until P5 HA.
- Cross-feature contracts (now reflected in those features' tickets). p2-worker-bound: add Email, EmailVerified and IdPIss to its Principal and build identity.Subject from them, so email blocks and `users:` rules keep working in require mode; require typ=wt+jwt and ver=1; deny tokens whose act.sub agent is disabled in the bundle. p2-signed-bundles: carry `tokenIssuer`, so workers take iss from the signed bundle. p2-key-manager: mint only with a kid already in the served JWKS (on first key creation, refresh the policy server before the first mint), and read the overlap floor from tokenService.ttl. p2-agent-registry: require or derive a kid for each JWK. p2-security-tests: add the stolen-token-on-another-port and replay-after-restart cases.

## Done when

On a CP with --state-dir, `tokenService.enabled: true` and an https issuer, a token key from p2-key-manager, an `identity` block that points at Dex (the p1-dex LDAP recipe), and an agent registered with a public JWK and allowed_groups: a user in an allowed group exchanges a Dex ID token (azp agent-harness) and a fresh agent assertion at POST /oauth2/token. The CP returns a typ wt+jwt token that verifies against /.well-known/jwks.json, carries the specified claims, and has exp = min(iat+15m, subject exp). Each specified invalid input (replayed jti including after a restart, alg none or HS256, an embedded-key header, wrong aud, an unknown or disabled agent, an expired or wrong-azp subject, a user blocked by sub or verified email, a user outside allowed_groups, a revoked session, an out-of-range scope or audience) gets its RFC 6749/8693 error and closed reason, and no token. Unauthenticated floods from one IP get 429 without using a real agent's budget. IdP unreachable with a cold cache, a missing token key, and a block-store error each return 503. Every authenticated outcome has a token_events row and a warden.token.v1 log line, and no token, subject_token or client_assertion appears in any row, log or label. With the service disabled the endpoint returns 404 and /policy is byte-identical.

### 1/7 · W-P2-TOKX-01

**Add private_key_jwt client assertion verification**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#82](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/82)

Add compact-JWS helpers to internal/keys and `VerifyClientAssertion` in new package internal/tokensvc. The token endpoint uses them to authenticate an agent from its signed assertion against the registry JWKs. The rules are strict: alg is bound to the key type, embedded-key headers are rejected, aud comes from config, and replay is checked per agent in cpstate, so a stolen or forged assertion cannot be reused. Nothing is mounted, so behaviour does not change.

**Requirements**

- New internal/keys/jws.go: `ParseCompact(raw string) (Header, payload, signingInput, sig []byte, error)` (3 base64url segments, strict) and `SignCompact(ctx, Signer, Header, claims any) (string, error)`. Only EdDSA and ES256 (raw r||s) are allowed. none, HS*, RS*, and crit/jku/jwk/x5u/x5c headers are rejected.
- `VerifyClientAssertion(ctx, raw string) (Client{AgentID, KID, JKT string}, error)` returns `*tokensvc.Error{Code: invalid_client, Reason}`. The assertion is capped at 8 KiB, iss must pass agentid.ValidID (W-P2-AREG-01) before lookup, and the clock is injected.
- Key selection: kid is required and must equal a registry JWK's kid or its RFC 7638 thumbprint (agentreg.Store.Get). alg must match the key type (OKP Ed25519 -> EdDSA, EC P-256 -> ES256) and the alg stored for that key in the registry (agent_keys.alg). The signature is checked with keys.Verify.
- Claims: iss==sub==agent id. aud is a single value (a string, or an array of one) equal to the configured issuer or `<issuer>/oauth2/token`; the CP never derives it from the request. exp and iat are required, exp-iat <= 5m, exp > now-60s, iat and nbf <= now+60s. jti is 1-128 printable characters. An optional form client_id must equal iss.
- Replay: cpstate migration `tokensvc/0001` adds `token_assertion_jti(agent_id TEXT, jti_hash TEXT, expires_at INTEGER, PRIMARY KEY(agent_id, jti_hash))` behind a `ReplayStore{Consume, Purge}` interface. The row is inserted only after the signature, time and status checks pass, using one INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and RowsAffected. Only sha256(jti) is stored.
- Unknown agent, unknown kid, bad signature and disabled agent all return the same invalid_client error, and an unknown agent still does a dummy verify so timing does not reveal which agent ids exist. Each case keeps its own reason (agent_unknown, unknown_kid, bad_signature, agent_disabled, replay, wrong_aud, expired, lifetime_too_long, alg_not_allowed, malformed, too_large) for logs and metrics only.
- JKT is the computed RFC 7638 thumbprint of the verifying JWK (keys.Thumbprint, the same value agentreg.Thumbprints serves to workers), never the header kid. The raw assertion never appears in errors, logs or test output; jti appears only as an 8-hex hash prefix.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/keys/jws.go with ParseCompact/SignCompact and tests against RFC 8037 (Ed25519) and RFC 7515 (ES256) vectors plus header-rejection cases.
2. New internal/tokensvc/errors.go: `OAuthCode` (invalid_request, invalid_client, invalid_grant, unauthorized_client, invalid_scope, invalid_target, unsupported_grant_type, temporarily_unavailable), the closed `Reason` enum and `type Error{Code, Reason}`.
3. New internal/tokensvc/replay.go: `ReplayStore` interface and its SQLite implementation registering cpstate migration `tokensvc/0001` (cpstate.Migration from W-P1-SSO-01).
4. New internal/tokensvc/assertion.go: `AssertionVerifier{Agents agentreg.Store; Replay ReplayStore; Issuer string; Now func() time.Time; Skew, MaxAge time.Duration}` with VerifyClientAssertion in the order parse -> lookup -> alg/key -> signature -> claims -> status -> replay.
5. Tests in new internal/tokensvc/assertion_test.go: a table test for every reason, a -race replay test, and a purge test with a fake clock.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Valid EdDSA and ES256 assertions return the agent id and a JKT equal to the keys thumbprint. alg none, HS256 signed with the public key bytes, RS256, an ES256 header on an Ed25519 key, a jwk or jku header, a missing kid and an unknown kid are each rejected with the matching reason: `go test ./internal/tokensvc -run TestVerifyClientAssertion`.
- [ ] Fifty goroutines submitting one valid assertion produce exactly one success and 49 replay failures, and a later sequential reuse also fails: `go test -race ./internal/tokensvc -run TestAssertionReplay`.
- [ ] aud ["<issuer>","https://other"] is rejected with wrong_aud and `<issuer>/oauth2/token` is accepted. exp-iat=6m gives lifetime_too_long, iss!=sub gives wrong_iss, and exp 2m in the past gives expired: `go test ./internal/tokensvc -run TestAssertionClaims`.
- [ ] A correctly signed assertion from a disabled agent returns agent_disabled, an unknown agent returns agent_unknown, and neither inserts a token_assertion_jti row.
- [ ] After the fake clock passes exp+60s, Purge removes the row, and the SQLite file contains no raw jti: `go test ./internal/tokensvc -run TestAssertionJTIPurge`.

**Depends on:** [`W-P2-AREG-01`](agent-registry.md#17--w-p2-areg-01) Add internal/agentreg store, schema and validation; [`W-P2-KEYS-01`](key-management.md#17--w-p2-keys-01) Add internal/keys Signer, JWK and RFC 7638 kid helpers; [`W-P1-SSO-01`](console-sso-rbac.md#111--w-p1-sso-01) Add internal/cpstate SQLite state store with migrations

### 2/7 · W-P2-TOKX-02

**Implement token exchange policy checks and JWT minting**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#83](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/83)

Add `Service.Exchange` in internal/tokensvc. It authenticates the agent (TOKX-01) and verifies the subject with the P1 `identity.NewOIDCVerifier` and `SubjectFrom`, accepting only status valid. It then checks the block list through `controlplane.BlockStore` (not a policy version), the agent's allowed groups and scope, and mints a typed, agent-bound JWT with the purpose=token signer. Every failure maps to a closed OAuth error, and any store or key failure fails closed. Nothing is mounted yet.

**Requirements**

- `Service.Exchange(ctx, ExchangeRequest{ClientAssertion, SubjectToken, SubjectTokenType, Scope, Audience, RequestedTokenType}) (*Issued, error)` dispatches on subject_token_type through a `SubjectResolver` map (id_token in P2; W-P4-DGR-04 adds grant). Unknown types give invalid_request/unsupported_token_type, and an audience other than warden-worker gives invalid_target.
- Subject: an identity.Verifier built with identity.NewOIDCVerifier from the served `identity` settings, with AllowedAZP set to tokenService.allowedAZP (default [agent-harness]). Only Status valid with a non-nil identity.SubjectFrom continues. expired -> invalid_grant/subject_expired; invalid -> invalid_grant/subject_invalid; unverified -> temporarily_unavailable/idp_unavailable.
- Block list: a tokensvc-owned `BlockChecker{IsBlocked(ctx, sub, email string) (bool, error)}`, with the adapter in new internal/controlplane/blockchecker.go over controlplane.BlockStore and the W-P1-BLOCK-07 snapshot (tokensvc never imports controlplane). Sub matches exactly; lowercase email matches only when EmailVerified. A match gives invalid_grant/user_blocked, and a read error gives temporarily_unavailable/block_store_unavailable.
- Agent and scope: re-read the agent and require status active. Subject groups intersect allowed_groups, otherwise unauthorized_client/group_not_allowed. Scope grammar `^[a-z0-9:._-]{1,64}$`, at most 16 tokens, and a subset of the agent's allowed_scopes (an omitted scope gives allowed_scopes; an empty list gives no scope claim), otherwise invalid_scope/scope_not_allowed.
- Minting with keys.SignCompact and the KeySet active signer. Header {alg, kid, typ: wt+jwt}. Claims ver=1, iss, aud=warden-worker, sub, idp_iss, email and email_verified (verified only), groups, groups_truncated, act.sub, sid, idp_sid (when present), jti (128-bit random), iat, nbf=iat, exp=min(iat+ttl, subject exp), scope and cnf.jkt, in a new `identity.WardenClaims` type that W-P2-WBND-01 can reuse. Tokens over 12 KiB give token_too_large, and keys.ErrNoActiveKey gives temporarily_unavailable/signer_unavailable. It mints only with a kid already present in the token JWKS the policy server last served (bundle `tokenJWKS` section and /.well-known/jwks.json); on first key creation the CP refreshes the policy server before the first mint.
- Sessions: cpstate migration `tokensvc/0002` adds `token_sessions(sid PK, idp_iss, sub, agent_id, created_at, last_used_at, revoked_at)` (not the W-P1-SSO-04 `sessions` table) behind `SessionStore{Touch, Revoke, RevokeAll, Purge}`. The sid is `wts_` plus 128-bit base64url, reused within 12h idle and 7d absolute. After a revoke, a subject token issued at or before revoked_at gives invalid_grant/session_revoked, and a later one starts a new sid.
- Exchange p99 is at most 25ms with a warm JWKS. Issued carries only the token plus {sub, agent, sid, jti, kid, exp, scope}; no subject_token, assertion or minted token is logged.

**Implementation plan**

1. 5. New internal/controlplane/blockchecker.go: the adapter from BlockStore to tokensvc.BlockChecker (not wired yet).

- [ ] A user blocked by sub, and a user blocked by an email-only entry with a verified email, both get invalid_grant/user_blocked. An unverified email does not match, and a BlockChecker error gives temporarily_unavailable with no token: `go test ./internal/tokensvc -run TestExchangeBlockedUser`.

### 3/7 · W-P2-TOKX-03

**Mount POST /oauth2/token with RFC 8693 request parsing and config**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#84](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/84)

Add the CP-local `tokenService:` config block and the HTTP handler that exposes Service.Exchange at `POST /oauth2/token`, plus RFC 8414 discovery metadata so harnesses do not hard-code the endpoint. The route sits outside the console session, CSRF and worker-token middleware and is classified in the W-P1-SSO-05 route table. With the block absent or disabled, both routes return 404 and nothing else changes. There is no CLI flag; the config key is the only switch.

**Requirements**

- Config: new internal/config/tokenservice.go `TokenServiceConfig` on `Policy.TokenService` with `json:"-"`, accepted by rawConfig under KnownFields(true), and new `config.LoadTokenService(path)` called on `--config` (the LoadConsole pattern). Keys and defaults as in the feature design: enabled false, issuer, ttl 15m (1m-15m), assertionMaxAge 5m, clockSkew 60s, allowedAZP [agent-harness], session {idle 12h, absolute 168h}, rateLimit {perIP "120/minute", perAgent "300/minute", perUser "30/minute", maxInFlight 64} with each rate in the `N/second|minute|hour` grammar of policy.ParseRateLimit, and eventRetention 720h.
- Validation: when enabled, issuer is required and must be an absolute https URL with no trailing slash (http only for loopback or allowInsecureIssuer, which logs a warning). Startup fails with an actionable error without --state-dir, without a served `identity` issuer, when `keys.enabled` is false or the token KeySet cannot load, or when `keys.token.overlap` is below ttl + 2m (worker skew plus one long-poll). One INFO line logs enabled, issuer and ttl.
- Route: `POST /oauth2/token` is registered in Server.Handler only when the service is built (otherwise 404); other methods get 405 with Allow: POST. It is outside dash.Handler, CSRF and WorkerAuthenticator, and is classified in the W-P1-SSO-05/AAUD-02 route table as assertion-authenticated with Audited:false. Session cookies and `wwt_` or `wak_` (apikeys.LooksLikeKey) bearers are never accepted as client auth; any Authorization header is rejected with invalid_request.
- Parsing: only application/x-www-form-urlencoded, http.MaxBytesReader at 32 KiB, no query-string parameters, no duplicate parameters, no Authorization header. grant_type must be token-exchange (otherwise unsupported_grant_type) and client_assertion_type must be jwt-bearer (otherwise invalid_client). actor_token and resource give invalid_request.
- Responses: JSON {error, error_description=reason}. 400 for invalid_request, invalid_grant, unauthorized_client, invalid_scope, invalid_target and unsupported_grant_type; 401 for invalid_client; 503 temporarily_unavailable with Retry-After. Every response has Content-Type application/json, Cache-Control: no-store and Pragma: no-cache. Success is 200 {access_token, issued_token_type, token_type: Bearer, expires_in = exp-iat, scope when non-empty}.
- Discovery: `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` returns issuer, token_endpoint, jwks_uri, grant_types_supported, token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported [private_key_jwt] and token_endpoint_auth_signing_alg_values_supported [EdDSA, ES256], only when enabled.
- Back-compat: when disabled, the route set, /policy bytes and every existing response are unchanged, and no tokensvc migrations run.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/config/tokenservice.go with TokenServiceConfig, defaults, validation and LoadTokenService; extend rawConfig and add TestTokenServiceNotOnWire and TestWritersPreserveTokenServiceBlock.
2. New internal/controlplane/tokenservice.go: `(s *Server) handleToken` and `handleASMetadata`, with the tokensvc.Error -> HTTP mapping.
3. internal/controlplane/controlplane.go: add `Config.Tokens *tokensvc.Service` and mount both routes in Server.Handler() when it is non-nil; add the routes to the authz route table in internal/controlplane/authz.go (W-P1-SSO-05).
4. cmd/proxy/controlplane.go: when tokenService.enabled, build identity.NewOIDCVerifier from the served identity settings, the token KeySet from the shared keys.Manager (controlplane.Config.Keys, W-P2-KEYS-02), the agentreg SQLite store, the BlockChecker adapter and tokensvc.New, and register the tokensvc migrations with cpstate.Open.
5. Tests: new internal/controlplane/tokenservice_test.go with a fake Service, internal/config tests, and a cmd/proxy startup test.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] grant_type=password returns 400 unsupported_grant_type. A JSON Content-Type, query-string parameters and a duplicate subject_token each return 400 invalid_request, and GET returns 405 with Allow: POST: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestTokenEndpointRequestValidation`.
- [ ] With a fake Service that succeeds, the response is 200 with Cache-Control: no-store, Pragma: no-cache, expires_in equal to exp-iat, issued_token_type jwt and token_type Bearer: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestTokenEndpointSuccess`.
- [ ] Every tokensvc error code maps to its documented status, 503 responses carry Retry-After, and error_description contains only enum reasons. A 33 KiB body returns 400 without calling the Service, and a valid console session cookie with no client_assertion returns 401 invalid_client: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestTokenEndpointErrorMapping`.
- [ ] With tokenService absent or enabled=false, POST /oauth2/token and the discovery URL return 404 and /policy is byte-identical. ttl 16m and a non-loopback http issuer are rejected at load, and enabling without --state-dir fails startup: `go test ./internal/config -run TestTokenServiceConfig` and `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneTokenService`.
- [ ] The discovery document lists token_endpoint `<issuer>/oauth2/token` and the private_key_jwt method, and the route-table coverage test passes: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestASMetadata|TestAuthzRouteCoverage'`.

### 4/7 · W-P2-TOKX-04

**Add rate limits, issuance records and metrics for token exchange**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#85](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/85)

Add the three-stage rate limits, so an unauthenticated caller cannot drain a real agent's or user's budget, and record every authenticated outcome in a prunable cpstate table plus a `warden.token.v1` JSON line. Issuance stays out of the hash-chained admin audit, because P1 never chains requests without a session and machine traffic would flood the admin chain. Recording fails closed: if the row cannot be written, no token is released.

**Requirements**

- Export `policy.ParseRateLimit` from internal/policy/policy.go (grammar unchanged, `N/second|minute|hour`) with a test. New internal/tokensvc/ratelimit.go: a token-bucket `Limiter.Allow(key, now) (ok bool, retryAfter time.Duration)` with a 10k-key LRU and idle eviction.
- Order: the per-client-IP limiter (default 120/minute; client IP from RemoteAddr or console.trustedProxies as in W-P1-AAUD-02) and the maxInFlight cap (default 64) run in handleToken before parsing. The per-agent limiter (default 300/minute) runs inside Exchange after the assertion verifies, and the per-user limiter on (idp_iss, sub) (default 30/minute) after the subject verifies. A limit hit gives 429 {"error":"rate_limited"} with integer Retry-After.
- Records: cpstate migration `tokensvc/0003` adds `token_events(id, ts, outcome, reason, agent_id, sub_hmac, sid, jti, kid, exp, scope)`. sub_hmac is HMAC-SHA256 with a per-CP random salt stored in cpstate. A row is written for every issuance and for every denial after the assertion verified, before the response is sent.
- If the row write fails, return 503 temporarily_unavailable/event_store_unavailable and release no token. Rows older than tokenService.eventRetention (default 720h) are pruned, together with expired token_assertion_jti and token_sessions rows, from the retention ticker in Server.Start.
- Each recorded outcome also emits one slog JSON line `msg=token_exchange schema=warden.token.v1` with sub, agent, sid, jti, kid, outcome, reason and exp. Unauthenticated failures write no row; they get a WARN line rate-limited to once per reason and client IP per minute, and a counter.
- Nothing in rows, logs or labels contains subject_token, client_assertion, the issued token, the Authorization header or the group list.
- Metrics: a nil-safe tokensvc.Metrics with in-memory counters `warden_cp_tokens_issued_total{agent}` and `warden_cp_tokens_denied_total{reason}` and a `warden_cp_token_exchange_seconds` histogram, following W-P1-WTOK-02. reason is the closed enum and agent is a registered id or `unknown`. They are exported when W-P5-RETN-06 adds the CP /metrics endpoint.
- The closed tokensvc Reason enum is exactly: malformed, too_large, alg_not_allowed, unknown_kid, bad_signature, wrong_iss, wrong_aud, expired, lifetime_too_long, replay, agent_unknown, agent_disabled, unsupported_token_type, invalid_target, subject_invalid, subject_expired, idp_unavailable, user_blocked, block_store_unavailable, group_not_allowed, scope_not_allowed, session_revoked, token_too_large, signer_unavailable, event_store_unavailable and rate_limited. It is the label set of warden_cp_tokens_denied_total and token_events.reason, is listed in docs/token-service.md, and p2-security-tests pins it.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/policy/policy.go: rename parseRateLimit to ParseRateLimit and update its callers; add a test in internal/policy/policy_test.go.
2. New internal/tokensvc/ratelimit.go and ratelimit_test.go with the token bucket and LRU.
3. internal/tokensvc/service.go: add the `Limiter` hooks after VerifyClientAssertion and after subject resolution, and a `Recorder` interface called before Exchange returns.
4. New internal/tokensvc/events.go: the SQLite Recorder (migration `tokensvc/0003`), the salt, the slog emitter and Purge. New internal/tokensvc/metrics.go.
5. internal/controlplane/tokenservice.go: the pre-auth IP limiter and in-flight cap. internal/controlplane/controlplane.go: call the tokensvc Purge methods from the retention ticker in Server.Start.
6. Tests in internal/tokensvc and internal/controlplane, using a fake clock and canary token strings.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] With perAgent 30/minute, the 31st verified exchange for one agent within a minute returns 429 with Retry-After >= 1, and one more request succeeds after 2s on the fake clock: `go test ./internal/tokensvc -run TestRateLimitBuckets`.
- [ ] 200 requests from one IP with forged assertions claiming agent A get 429 after the 120th, and a genuine request for agent A from another IP still returns 200: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestTokenRateLimitForgedAgentNoDoS`.
- [ ] One successful and one group_not_allowed exchange each write exactly one token_events row and one warden.token.v1 line, and write no admin_audit row. 100 bad-signature requests write zero rows and raise the bad_signature counter by 100: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestTokenEventsRecorded`.
- [ ] Canary strings for subject_token, client_assertion and the minted token appear in no row, slog output or metric label: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestTokenEventsNoLeak`.
- [ ] With the event store forced to fail, a valid exchange returns 503 and the body has no access_token: `go test ./internal/tokensvc -run TestExchangeEventStoreFailClosed`.
- [ ] The set of denied-counter reasons equals the tokensvc Reason enum: `go test ./internal/tokensvc -run TestMetricReasonsBounded`.

### 5/7 · W-P2-TOKX-05

**Add token service end-to-end integration test**

Type **test** · Size **M** · Issue [#86](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/86)

Prove the exchange end to end in Go tests. The main test uses the in-process `fakes.OIDCIssuer` from W-P1-VRFY-11, so it runs in the default gate with no Docker; an L2 subtest on the shared identity stack of W-P1-DEX-04 uses a real Dex token of the seeded LDAP user alice. The test reuses the existing Dex clients and does not change Dex config. It covers the happy path, the main denials, replay after a CP restart, revocation and the IdP-down 503.

**Requirements**

- New test `TestTokenExchangeE2E` in internal/controlplane/tokenexchange_e2e_test.go (no build tag, no Docker), run by the default `go test -race ./...` stage of scripts/check.sh.
- Start the CP in process with a temp --state-dir, tokenService enabled, and the identity issuer pointed at the in-process issuer (azp agent-harness, groups eng). Seed an agent with an Ed25519 public JWK through agentreg.Store.Create.
- Happy path: build an assertion with keys.SignCompact, exchange it, fetch /.well-known/jwks.json (W-P2-KEYS-04), and verify the token with keys.ParseCompact and keys.Verify. Check typ, iss, aud, sub, idp_iss, email, act.sub, cnf.jkt, sid, and exp <= subject exp.
- Negative subtests check the OAuth error, HTTP status and token_events row count for each case: replayed assertion (also after restarting the CP on the same state dir), blocked user (BlockStore.Add), disabled agent (SetStatus), user outside allowed_groups, expired subject, wrong assertion aud, and a revoked session (W-P2-TOKX-07).
- Degraded subtest: with the issuer stopped and a cold JWKS cache, the exchange returns 503 temporarily_unavailable.
- L2 subtest `TestTokenExchangeDex` in test/e2e/identity/token_exchange_test.go (`//go:build e2e`, shared stack from W-P1-DEX-04, run by `make e2e-identity-scenario NAME=TestTokenExchangeDex`): the `dexToken(t, "alice")` helper produces a real Dex token that exchanges successfully against the stack's CP (tokenService enabled in configs/config.e2e-identity-cp.yaml), and the resulting groups include warden-admins. No new Dex users, clients or trustedPeers are added.
- Test output never prints tokens. Captured CP logs are scanned for JWT-shaped strings.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/controlplane/tokenexchange_e2e_test.go using fakes.OIDCIssuer from W-P1-VRFY-11 (test/fakes/oidcissuer.go).
2. Helper to build controlplane.Server with tokenService, agentreg and BlockStore on a temp state dir, and to restart it on the same dir.
3. Happy-path, negative, restart, revoke and degraded subtests.
4. L2 Dex subtest in test/e2e/identity/token_exchange_test.go using the dexToken helper and the stack from W-P1-DEX-04.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run TestTokenExchangeE2E` passes on a machine without Docker, and `scripts/check.sh` is green.
- [ ] The verified token has typ wt+jwt, aud=warden-worker, act.sub equal to the agent id, cnf.jkt equal to the test key's RFC 7638 thumbprint, and exp-iat <= 900.
- [ ] Replay (before and after restart) gives 401 invalid_client, a blocked user 400 invalid_grant, a disabled agent 401 invalid_client, a user outside groups 400 unauthorized_client, an expired subject 400 invalid_grant, and a revoked session 400 invalid_grant.
- [ ] With the issuer stopped and a cold cache the response is 503, never 200.
- [ ] `make e2e-identity-scenario NAME=TestTokenExchangeDex` passes: alice's real Dex token exchanges successfully. Captured test and CP logs contain no substring starting with `eyJ`.

### 7/7 · W-P2-TOKX-07

**Add admin revocation for token sessions**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#254](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/254)

Add admin routes that revoke one token session, or all sessions for a user or an agent, so the key-rotation runbook (W-P2-KEYS-05) and incident response have a real 'revoke sessions' step. After a revoke the token service refuses further exchanges for that session; live tokens still expire within the TTL. The routes are admin-only and audited through the P1 admin audit middleware.

**Requirements**

- `POST /dashboard/api/token-sessions/{sid}/revoke` returns 204, or 404 for an unknown sid. `POST /dashboard/api/token-sessions/revoke` with {sub?, idp_iss?, agent_id?} (at least one field) returns 200 {revoked: n}. Both call SessionStore.Revoke or RevokeAll (W-P2-TOKX-02).
- `GET /dashboard/api/token-sessions?agent_id=&sub=` (admin) lists sid, agent_id, created_at, last_used_at and revoked_at, at most 200 per page.
- The routes are in the W-P1-SSO-05 authz table as admin-only, Scope ScopeNone (W-P2-APIK-02) and Audited:true, with target `token_sessions` and target_ref `sid:<sid>` or the filter. Editors and viewers get 403, and without --state-dir or with the service disabled the routes return 404.
- A revoke sets revoked_at and never deletes the row. Exchanges whose subject token was issued at or before revoked_at get invalid_grant/session_revoked, so the user must sign in again. A subject token issued after the revoke starts a new sid.
- No token value is shown or logged; the sid is not a credential.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/controlplane/tokensessions.go with the three handlers over tokensvc.SessionStore.
2. Register the routes in Server.Handler() when the token service is enabled and add them to internal/controlplane/authz.go.
3. Tests in new internal/controlplane/tokensessions_test.go for role checks, audit rows and the follow-up exchange.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] An admin revoke returns 204 and writes one admin_audit row with target token_sessions. An editor gets 403: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestTokenSessionRevoke`.
- [ ] After a revoke, Exchange for that session returns invalid_grant/session_revoked: `go test ./internal/tokensvc -run TestExchangeSessionID`.
- [ ] Revoke-all by agent_id revokes only that agent's sessions, and the response count matches.
- [ ] With tokenService disabled, every /dashboard/api/token-sessions route returns 404.
